source.record: [Mixed-level chains with up to exp((log N)^(2/3)) layers](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/ultimate-matching/#entry-2026-10-17-multilevel-chains)
source.label: Mixed-level chains with up to exp((log N)^(2/3)) layers

reviewer: Claude Code with sole fresh-context medium reviewer

claims.summary: On the event of lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (probability tending to one), at (4,4), for every dyadic delta_0 with kappa sqrt(log N/N) <= delta_0 <= 2^(-l_1), every fixed M in [1, 2e^16] and every nested chain g = delta_0 sum_{k <= K} y_k 1_{A_k} (A_1 containing ... containing A_K unions of cells, heights y_k >= 2e^16 otherwise arbitrary) with discrete cost sum_e delta_0^2 psi*_4(|Delta_e g|/(2 delta_0)) <= M (the goal's class has M = 2), its layers split into high H (y_k >= N^(1/3)), small S (not high, P(A_k) < 1) and large B (not high, P(A_k) >= 1), y_B = min over B: (a) c_k = delta_0 P(A_k) psi*_4(y_k/2) has sum_k c_k <= M and y_k delta_0 P(A_k) <= 4 c_k (log(y_k/2))^(-1/4); (b) for N large, if |S| <= N^(1/6)/(log N)^2 and log|B| <= (log N)^(2/3)(log(y_B/2))^(1/3) (no condition on H), then |D(g)| <= (17 M C_b + 1 + 6 M L_f) sqrt(N log N), C_b and L_f the constants of lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (b) and lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor; in particular when K <= N^(1/7) and log K <= (log N)^(2/3)(log(min_k y_k/2))^(1/3); (c) hence every grid function whose distinct values v_0 < ... < v_K are at least 2e^16 delta_0 apart, of cost at most M, whose layer-cake chain meets the conditions of (b), in particular with K <= e^((log N)^(2/3)), has the same bound.
claims.assessment: Working proof: the one-signed increments of nested sets and superadditivity of psi*_4 split the cost over the layers; psi*_4(t) >= (t/2)(log t)^(1/4) for t >= e^16; high layers (any number) by (a) and lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (b), small-perimeter layers by its (a), the others by lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (b) per layer, the monotone function x(2 log_2(4y/x) + 5)^(3/4) at x = 4 c_k (log(y_k/2))^(-1/4), and Jensen for the concave c (2 log_2(1/c))^(3/4) over the costs; the layer cake for (c).
claims.rationale: Extends lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d), proved at one level, to nested chains at mixed levels and so to grid functions with separated values, at the goal's order uniformly in a growing number of layers; the record's compositions (per layer, per dyadic height group, lem:discrete-flow-bound (c) split at one height) give this for boundedly many layers or height groups, and otherwise a factor growing with the number G of dyadic height groups, at least of order min{(G ln 2)^(1/4), (log N)^(1/8)}, or with the number of layers once a group exceeds the single-level conditions; chains with more large layers remain open.
claims.next_action: Bound chains with more large layers than log|B| <= (log N)^(2/3)(log(y_B/2))^(1/3), at growing multiplicity, by charging bundles of layers sharing a tube by their spread as lem:band-family-discrepancy (c) does for bands; on the matching side, bound the length of an optimal chain.

relationships: Its part (b) per layer, and its proof's form of the log factor.
Its (a) for small-perimeter layers and (c) for high layers.
Its (c), split at one height, bounds such chains with a loss of order (log N)^(1/8) at small multiplicity; the lemma removes the loss for its range of layer counts.
Its (d) is at one level with guides.
Its (c) bounds disjoint bands along graphs of bounded slope at mixed ramp gradients against Lebesgue measure, a different class; the template for the next attempt.
